findings.title: Center has no designed tension and uplift restraint
findings.finding: The straight two-inch tongues have no pegs, bolts, retained dovetail or other positive withdrawal restraint. Nominal contact does not close the central force path.
findings.action: Design the open-center drum/ring and its joints as one system. Evaluate a plain housed dovetail where radial withdrawal governs, with separate restraint against its insertion/removal direction. Do not assume an open-bottom polygon or plywood alone supplies the required ring action.

findings.title: Main-rafter tongue exceeds the receiver-based proportion
findings.finding: The generic width rule uses the 8-inch rafter: 8/3 = 2.667 inches. In a 6-inch receiving post, nominal cheeks are only (6 - 2.667)/2 = 1.667 inches before neighboring cuts. TFEC 1-2019 §§3.4.10–11 use the receiving member and require each cheek at least the mortise width for the prescribed tension-joint provisions.
findings.action: Redesign this joint from the receiving post and load demand. A broader head is not a remedy for thin cheeks. A dovetail is a different connection requiring its own neck, bearing and splitting/block-shear checks.

findings.title: Two-inch insertion is not a ready-made pegged tension joint
findings.finding: No peg location or end distance is modeled. For illustration, the TFEC full geometry factor calls for 4D loaded-end distance in a softwood tension member: a 3/4-inch peg alone needs 3 inches from peg center to the loaded end. The current two-inch tongue cannot provide that distance.
findings.action: Resolve species, peg diameter, receiving-face edge distances and joint arrangement together; do not simply drill the existing tongues. This comparison does not assign a capacity or prohibit every alternative tested detail.

findings.title: Outer seats carry gravity but do not lock against uplift
findings.finding: R0 bears across the 8 × 8 post head (64 in² nominal horizontal footprint). Each short rafter has approximately 12 in² of horizontal bearing on its ring beam. These are real support surfaces, not merely the colored cavity edge seen in the screenshot. No rated uplift or sliding restraint is modeled.
findings.action: Keep broad gravity bearing; check heel/block shear, remaining rafter section and the signed force direction. Retain or adjust the seat only after those checks. Add a designed restraint for force reversal; a deeper notch alone is not a solution.

findings.title: Braces, eave-ring joints and post bases need a complete lateral system
findings.finding: Braces use full-section diagonal sockets without a complete peg/housing design. Eave-ring joints share post heads with other cuts. No foundation anchorage is modeled. Enclosed walls are confirmed, but their sheathing and attachments are not.
findings.action: Trace wall/roof shear through collectors, braces or shear panels, post joints and foundations. Check both wind directions, load reversal, combined notches and erection stability.

findings.title: Cupola ceiling and roof require attachments
findings.finding: The horizontal half-inch plywood and eight exposed horizontal ceiling spokes now follow the user-confirmed arrangement. Ceiling spoke 4 × 6 sizes and roof-rafter 2 × 6 depths are assumptions. Center miters touch but do not themselves resist separation. Finish boards are not assigned an invented thickness.
findings.action: Design center and perimeter connections plus plywood grade, panel joints, edge blocking and fastening. Do not credit the plywood as a diaphragm until its complete boundary load path is specified.

findings.title: Earlier prototype is not verified stronger
findings.finding: The earlier model used algorithmic keys and larger-looking interlocks. Its own engineering review recorded severely reduced webs and unresolved raising/tool access. Those shapes were not a verified traditional joinery schedule.
findings.action: Retain useful viewing features and compare real housings/shoulders, but do not restore arbitrary keys as a structural fix.

findings.title: Geometric audit has a defined limit
findings.finding: Positive-volume pair overlaps, registered contact and connected meshes pass. The separate unfilled-socket volume diagnostics are nonzero and numerically inconsistent under rotation; complete cavity closure is not certified.
findings.action: Resolve socket-volume closure independently before any fabrication claim. The contact-area proxy in the fit report is a geometry diagnostic, not a structural bearing-capacity calculation.

load_coefficients.usage: For a uniform pressure q in lb/ft² of horizontal projection, total vertical force equals q times plan area. Per-bay values apply only to a symmetric load accounting case, not individual joint reactions. Actual wind/snow are not assumed uniform or divided equally. Timber weight equals volume times confirmed density. No load magnitudes or capacities have been assigned.
